derivation: Read the third semicolon field General_Category in each versioned UnicodeData.txt, expand any matching First/Last range, retain exactly Mn/Mc/Me code points, then merge consecutive points into inclusive integer ranges. The identical15.0/15.1 range sets are stored once. This extraction did not import retrieval.tokens or unicodedata.category.
runtime_version_selection: Tests use unicodedata.unidata_version only to select the pinned external table; no category result from that module is an expected value.
casefold_source_use: The full C/F entries in the fetched CaseFolding files were reviewed only for representative literal order examples and to confirm all mappings are nonempty and shorter than the record marker. They are not stored as another general engine.

limits: The exhaustive assertion is Unicode mark deletion in anchored token contexts, including unassigned points and lone surrogates.
Literal mixed-script, ordering and token-boundary cases sample the unchanged downstream transformations; they do not exhaust all strings.
The actual catalogue/ranking comparison is a regression against an existing exposed frozen result, not a new independent linguistic or held-out benchmark.
No performance result or cached implementation output supplies expected semantics.
The semantic acceptance suite does not require memoization, so it can run unchanged before and after the optimization.

prerelease_fixture_review.review: Before the first test run, root identified that a JSON escaped surrogate pair is decoded by json.loads into one supplementary character.
prerelease_fixture_review.correction: Store explicit integer codepoints [65, 55357, 56832, 90]; the evaluator constructs the Python string with chr for each integer.
prerelease_fixture_review.unchanged_coverage: All-codepoint anchored classification, all lone surrogates, and the separate actual-emoji boundary case.
